guideTitle: 6 Best Electric Pruning Shears Under $100 in 2026
metaTitle: Best Electric Pruning Shears Under $100 in 2026
metaDescription: Six electric pruning shears and one mini chainsaw kit compared by cutting capacity and spare parts, for gardeners who cut thick branches.
introParagraphs: Once the budget reaches this level, pruners stop being about comfort alone and start being about reach. The tools here cut branches that a hand pruner would defeat: the thumb-thick limb of a fruit tree, the woody stem of an old lilac, the overgrown hedge you finally decided to tame. Capacity jumps past 2 inches on several models, and spare blades start to appear in the box.

That shift changes what you should check. A stronger motor is only half the story. You also want to know how many batteries you receive, whether a replacement blade is included and what kind of steel the blade uses, because wood this thick wears an edge faster. One kit in this guide even pairs a pruner with a mini chainsaw, which suits a different kind of yard.

Our approach is to read published specs and patterns in buyer feedback, not to claim hands-on testing. Treat capacity numbers as the best case on clean green wood. Seasoned or knotty branches reduce the practical limit, and the right habit is to stay a half inch below the stated maximum. That small margin protects both the blade and the motor, and it keeps the cut clean instead of ragged.

products.name: ANTTCTIG 2.75 Inch Brushless Electric Pruning Shears
products.description:
The ANTTCTIG 2.75 is the biggest cutter in the lineup, with a maximum opening of 2.75 inches or about 70mm. A 700W brushless motor drives the blades, and the listing says the SK7 steel is harder than the SK5 common on cheaper pruners, which should mean longer service life between sharpenings. Two 2.0Ah batteries and spare blades arrive together.

The tradeoff is that this much capacity can be overkill. If your branches are mostly thin, you will carry a heavier tool than you need. The listing also does not name a runtime figure or a specific blade steel grade beyond SK7, and ANTTCTIG is a less established name, so buyer feedback matters.

Compared with the ANTTCTIG 2.56, it adds almost a quarter inch of reach and a stronger motor. Compared with the PAOWAFOL at 2.1 inches, it takes bigger bites and comes with spares. It is the pick for anyone with serious fruit trees or overgrown shrubs who wants the largest opening available at this level.

products.name: ANTTCTIG 2.56 Inch Electric Pruning Shears
products.description:
This is the slightly smaller sibling, and for many gardeners it is the better buy. A 2.56 inch maximum opening handles heavy-duty trimming, and two settings, 1.97 inches and 2.56 inches, let you match the opening to the branch. The premium SK7 steel blade is described as sharper and more durable than SK5.

Two batteries and spare blades come in the package, which makes this a ready-to-use kit instead of a tool you must expand with purchases. The caution is the brand: ANTTCTIG is less established, so check how current buyers describe support. It is also overkill if your branches stay thin.

Compared with the 2.75 inch version, it gives up about a fifth of an inch of reach for a slightly more manageable tool. Compared with the MODOFO 2.1, it has a bigger opening and spare blades. It is the choice that balances capacity, extras and confidence, which is why it leads for value.

products.name: MODOFO 2.1 Inch Brushless Electric Pruning Shears
products.description:
The MODOFO 2.1 is the versatile mid-range choice. It cuts up to 2.1 inches on the thick setting and drops to 1.6 inches for precise work, so a single tool covers a lot of ground. A brushless motor and an LCD display come standard, and two 2.0Ah batteries mean a drained pack does not end the day.

The listing does not give a runtime number, which makes it harder to compare battery life against rivals, and the generic brand name leaves some uncertainty about long-term support. Those are the usual compromises at this tier.

Compared with the ANTTCTIG 2.56, it gives up roughly half an inch of reach and does not list spare blades. Compared with the 1.4 inch MODOFO, it adds capacity and a second mode. It is a good fit for people who want a display, two modes and sensible capacity without moving into the biggest tools.

products.name: PAOWAFOL 2.1 Inch Cordless Electric Pruning Shears
products.description:
The PAOWAFOL separates two numbers that many listings blur together: a 1.6 inch cutting capacity and a 2.1 inch maximum opening. In practice the jaws open wide but clean cutting is rated for 1.6 inches, which is worth remembering when you size your branches. A brushless motor and an LCD display come with it.

The headline claim is battery life. Two 2000mAh batteries are said to deliver 3000+ cuts per charge, a stronger figure than the SEESII's 2000+ cuts, though it is the maker's claim and real results depend on wood thickness. That makes it attractive for long days on moderate branches.

Compared with the MODOFO 2.1, it states its capacity more honestly but cuts less thick wood. Compared with the ANTTCTIG models, it lacks spare blades in the listing and tops out below them. Pick it if runtime matters more than the biggest possible opening.

products.name: SEESII 2-in-1 Mini Chainsaw and Pruning Shears Combo
products.description:
The SEESII combo is two tools in one box: a 6 inch mini cordless chainsaw and a 1.2 inch electric pruner. Both run on 600W brushless motors, and two 2000mAh lithium batteries with a fast charger keep work going, since you can use one while the other charges. The chainsaw weighs about 3.3 pounds and carries a dual-switch safety lock.

This kit solves a different problem than the other picks. When you have thin branches and the occasional log or thick limb, the pruner handles the former and the chainsaw the latter. The compromise is that the pruner opens only 1.2 inches, much less than the 2 inch tools here, and the chainsaw has a short blade. Check the listing for the exact accessories included.

Compared with the ANTTCTIG models, it cuts thinner stems but adds a saw. Compared with the 1.4 inch MODOFO, it offers a smaller pruner but a second tool. It is a good fit for yard cleanup where one tool never does the whole job.

products.name: MODOFO Upgraded 1.4 Inch Electric Pruning Shears
products.description:
The 1.4 inch MODOFO is the baseline against which the bigger tools are measured. A 450W brushless motor and an SK5 blade cut up to about 1.4 inches, adjustable modes allow smaller bites, and an LCD display shows live status. Two 2.0Ah batteries are packed in, so you can keep pruning while one recharges.

It is the lowest-capacity pick here, which means it will not handle the thick limbs the 2 inch tools target. The generic listing name also invites a check on recent buyer feedback. For roses, hedges and trained shrubs it is entirely adequate, though.

Compared with the MODOFO 2.1, you lose seven tenths of an inch of reach. Compared with the SEESII combo's 1.2 inch pruner, you gain capacity but not a saw. Buy it as a sensible starting point if your branches stay modest and you do not want to pay for capacity you will not use.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Listings use two different numbers: the maximum jaw opening and the diameter the blade cuts cleanly. They can differ by half an inch. The PAOWAFOL separates them as a 1.6 inch cutting capacity and 2.1 inch opening, while the ANTTCTIG 2.75 cites its opening. Stay about half an inch below any stated figure on seasoned wood.

Harder steel holds an edge longer on thick, dense wood. SK7 is described as harder than SK5, and both ANTTCTIG models use it. The MODOFO models use SK5, which is still good for general use. If you cut a lot of dry wood, favor SK7.

Thick wood dulls blades quickly, so spares keep you cutting. Both ANTTCTIG models include spare blades, while the MODOFO and PAOWAFOL listings do not mention them. Buying spares later costs time and sometimes a mismatched fit. Count them as part of the value.

Two batteries let you swap and keep working. Cut counts are the maker's claims, but they tell you the scale: the PAOWAFOL states 3000+ cuts per charge from two 2000mAh packs. The SEESII combo includes two 2000mAh batteries and a fast charger. Plan for the real figure to be lower on thick wood.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Pruner versus saw for thick wood
buyingCriteria.explanation: Past about 2.5 inches a pruner struggles and a saw makes more sense. The SEESII combo pairs a 1.2 inch pruner with a 6 inch mini chainsaw, which covers both ends. If your yard has logs or firewood, a kit like this can be more useful than a pruner alone.

More capacity means a bigger motor and a heavier body. A heavier pruner tires the arm during a long session. The SEESII chainsaw weighs about 3.3 pounds, a figure that helps you judge a kit. Match the tool to your strength.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and cutting range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated cutting diameters and opening sizes. The ANTTCTIG 2.75 leads at 2.75 inches, followed by the ANTTCTIG 2.56 at 2.56 inches, the MODOFO 2.1 at 2.1 inches and the PAOWAFOL at a 1.6 inch rated cut. The 1.4 inch MODOFO and the 1.2 inch SEESII pruner trail.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade and what is in the box
howWeEvaluated.description: Steel grade and included spares drive this category. Both ANTTCTIG models scored best with SK7 blades and spares. The MODOFO and PAOWAFOL listings do not mention spares, so they scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at battery count and any stated cut figures. The PAOWAFOL's 3000+ cuts claim led, with the SEESII's two 2000mAh packs and fast charger close behind. Listings with no runtime figure scored neutrally.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: Displays, mode switching and safety locks matter. The MODOFO models and PAOWAFOL offer LCD displays, and the SEESII chainsaw has a dual-switch safety lock. We did not test them, so these are editorial assessments.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the budget
howWeEvaluated.description: Since every pick sits under the cap, value means capacity and extras for the price. The ANTTCTIG 2.56 leads for balance, the MODOFO 1.4 for entry value and the SEESII combo for versatility.

faq.q: What is the difference between cutting capacity and opening?
faq.a: Opening is how far the jaws spread, while capacity is the thickness the blade cuts cleanly. The PAOWAFOL lists 1.6 inches and 2.1 inches respectively. Use the cutting capacity to judge branches.
On thick or dry wood, yes. Both ANTTCTIG models include them, which saves a separate purchase. Without spares, a dull blade can leave you waiting for a replacement.
SK7 is described as harder than SK5, so it should hold an edge longer on dense wood. For casual trimming either is fine. It matters most if you cut a lot of thick branches.
For branches within their capacity, yes, and they are faster and cleaner. Past about 2.75 inches you need a saw. The SEESII kit adds a mini chainsaw for that gap.

faq.q: How safe is the SEESII chainsaw?
faq.a: The listing mentions a dual-switch safety lock and a weight of about 3.3 pounds. A chainsaw is still a chainsaw, so wear eye protection and gloves. Read the instructions before first use.
They are the maker's claims, like 3000+ cuts on the PAOWAFOL and 2000+ on the SEESII. Real counts drop on thick wood. Treat them as a rough scale, not a promise.

faq.q: Which is best for a beginner?
faq.a: The ANTTCTIG 2.56 or the MODOFO 2.1 are good starting points because they offer two modes and sensible capacity. The 1.4 inch MODOFO is simpler if your branches are modest.
